lines.trans: Stop doing things you hate doing—you have done more than enough up to now.

Oh, I got that playing soccer earlier. Where did you learn first aid like this?
When I get hurt performing overseas or out in the provinces, there is no time for hospitals, so I handle this much myself.

meanings.note: Used as casual question (겁나?).

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

다치다.gloss: to get hurt, to be injured

examples.trans: Just stand up to her head-on and walk out of that agency!

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

meanings.note: Used as casual -잖아 (멍들잖아.).

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.trans: If we prepare (without fail, unconditionally), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.
